brief: Find illustration-style views of Brooklyn brownstones / classic Brooklyn residential streetscapes as a more characterful alternative to the current bridge plate.

current_plate.title: The Great East River Suspension Bridge ... View from Brooklyn, looking west
current_plate.note: Compliant illustration of the Brooklyn Bridge from the Brooklyn shore. Options below explore a more residential, brownstone-leaning Brooklyn character.

sourcing_note: Colour, public-domain ILLUSTRATIONS of true brownstone ROWS (stoops, tree-lined blocks in Park Slope / Bed-Stuy / Brooklyn Heights) are extremely scarce: the recognised brownstone-row images from that era are almost all photographs (e.g. Berenice Abbott's 'Changing New York' series on Commons) or drypoints/etchings by artists still in copyright (Martin Lewis, Armin Landeck). The genuine PD/CC0 ILLUSTRATIONS of Brooklyn residential streets that do exist are the two Francis Guy winter street scenes and Miklos Suba's Precisionist neighbourhood views. Candidates below are the best illustration-and-Brooklyn matches found; each is flagged for how closely it meets the 'brownstone' brief.

excluded_examples: Berenice Abbott, 'Changing New York' Brooklyn series (Willow Place, Columbia Heights nos., Talman St) NYPL b13668355 - genuine brownstone rows but PHOTOGRAPHS.
'210-220 Columbia Heights' - modern colour PHOTOGRAPH of a real brownstone row (CC BY-SA).
Met 'Scenes of Old New York' etchings (The Crooked Stoop, etc.) - illustrated stoops/old houses but MANHATTAN, not Brooklyn.
'View of New York from Brooklyn Heights' (Currier / Met) - harbour skyline view, overlaps existing plates, not residential.
recommendation: guy-winter-scene-brooklyn-museum.jpg - Francis Guy's 'Winter Scene in Brooklyn' (Brooklyn Museum). It is the single most characterful, unmistakably-Brooklyn residential street ILLUSTRATION in the public domain: colour, high quality, clean licence, and a lively actual Brooklyn streetscape of houses, shops and stoops. It is wood-frame old Brooklyn rather than brownstones, but no colour PD illustration of a true brownstone row exists. If a brick 'row' look is essential, the runner-up is suba-atlantic-avenue-brooklyn.jpg (colour Brooklyn brick row, but commercial and low-res) or guy-winter-scene-brooklyn-dallas.jpg (has a brownstone-fronted stoop house).

round2.brief: Dig deeper for MORE options reading specifically as Brooklyn BROWNSTONE ROWS (brick/brownstone row houses, stoops, tree-lined residential blocks). Try pre-1929 colour chromolithograph postcards of residential streets/parkways, WPA/Federal Art Project prints of Brooklyn streets, and genuinely PD etchings/lithographs of stoops and rows. Prefer colour, accept strong monochrome brownstone-row prints.
round2.sources_searched: The Met Open Access API (Drawings & Prints), Smithsonian American Art Museum (via Wikimedia Commons), Library of Congress, Wikimedia Commons (searches + category trees), Digital Commonwealth / Boston Public Library Tichnor Brothers postcard collection, NYPL Digital Collections. Extensive querying across all of these.
round2.sourcing_note: Round 1's core conclusion holds: there is essentially NO clean-public-domain COLOUR ILLUSTRATION of a true Brooklyn brownstone row. The colour-postcard route fails on two counts: (a) the surviving colour Brooklyn postcards on the clean-licence platforms are overwhelmingly landmarks, parks, the Museum, the plaza and businesses, not leafy brownstone residential blocks; and (b) the ones that DO show streets are almost all either photographs / photochroms / real-photo cards (disallowed by the illustration rule) or Tichnor 'linen' cards dated ca.1930-1945, i.e. post-1929 and only 'no known copyright restrictions' (a copyright flag, not clean PD). The genuinely NEW value found this round is on the WPA / print side: Ann Nooney's Federal Art Project lithographs of Brooklyn residential streets are the best 'brick row + stoops' SUBJECT match located in either round, but they carry a real licence question; and Joseph Pennell's 1909 charcoal drawing is impeccably PD but is almost certainly the MANHATTAN approach to the bridge, not Brooklyn. All candidates below are monochrome except the Miller watercolour, which is colour but a rural homestead rather than a brownstone row.
round2.licence_caveat_wpa: Ann Nooney (1900-1970) died only 56 years ago, so these prints are NOT public domain by author-death. The PD claim rests on the WPA/Federal Art Project argument (federally sponsored prints distributed without copyright notice). The Smithsonian American Art Museum and Wikimedia Commons treat them as public domain; however The Metropolitan Museum of Art, which holds the same Nooney lithographs, explicitly marks them isPublicDomain=false and provides NO open-access image. This is a genuine, unresolved copyright doubt - treat as BORDERLINE, not clean PD.

Impeccable licence but probably wrong borough.

also_investigated_and_rejected: Colour chromolithograph postcards of Eastern Parkway / Bedford Avenue / Prospect Park West / Ocean Parkway (NYPL, Wikimedia, Digital Commonwealth): those that surfaced show the Museum, the plaza, parks, churches, armouries and businesses - not brownstone residential rows - and the residential-street colour cards are either photographs/photochroms/real-photo (disallowed) or low-res.

Tichnor Brothers linen postcards (Boston Public Library / Digital Commonwealth): colour, but ca.1930-1945 (post-1929) and only 'no known copyright restrictions'; also no true Brooklyn brownstone-row card exists in the set (mostly businesses/landmarks). Copyright-flagged and off-subject.

Ann Nooney, 'Brooklyn Street' (Met 43.33.401) and 'Hillside Street' (Met 43.33.747): the most on-brief WPA titles, but the Met marks them not-PD and provides no downloadable image, so they cannot be used.
Detroit Publishing Co. photochroms of Brooklyn parkways (Library of Congress): colour but they are colourised PHOTOGRAPHS - disallowed by the illustration rule.
Museum of the City of New York 'Maple Street limestone residences' etc.: genuine brownstone/limestone rows but PHOTOGRAPHS with restrictive rights.
Robert Spencer, 'The White Tenement' (Brooklyn Museum): PD painting, but the subject is not Brooklyn (Spencer painted Pennsylvania mill-town tenements) and it is low-res.
Grand Army Plaza / Eastern Parkway colour postcard (Wikimedia): tiny (652x414) and a plaza/monument, not brownstones.
round2.recommendation: Top NEW pick: nooney-near-brooklyn-bridge.jpg (Ann Nooney, 'Near Brooklyn Bridge', SAAM/WPA). It is the single best 'brick row houses with stoops on a Brooklyn street' ILLUSTRATION found in either round - exactly the brownstone-row read the brief wants - IF the WPA/Federal Art Project public-domain argument is acceptable. Its licence is BORDERLINE (SAAM/Wikimedia say PD, the Met says not-PD, artist d.1970), so it should not be presented as clean PD. If a strictly clean licence is required, no new candidate beats round 1: Pennell is clean PD but almost certainly Manhattan, and Miller is clean PD colour but a rural homestead. In that case round 1's guy-winter-scene-brooklyn-museum.jpg remains the safest recommendation, with nooney-near-brooklyn-bridge.jpg as the more literally-brownstone alternative pending a licence decision.

round3.brief: Borough constraint RELAXED. The user now wants the 'brick row houses / brownstones' AESTHETIC and is happy with a MANHATTAN example if it looks right, so place-accuracy is secondary to the brownstone/brick-row look. Find 4-6 NEW illustration candidates that strongly read as NYC brownstone / brick row houses with stoops and iron railings, tree-lined residential blocks. Manhattan neighbourhoods (Harlem, Greenwich Village, Chelsea, Upper West Side, Gramercy, Murray Hill) explicitly encouraged alongside Brooklyn. Prefer colour, accept strong monochrome brownstone-row prints.
round3.sources_searched: The Met Open Access API (Drawings & Prints, dept 9), Wikimedia Commons (search + artist queries), Whitney Museum and National Gallery of Art open-access donations on Commons, Google Art Project, plus targeted checks of Smithsonian American Art Museum / Library of Congress leads. Focused on pre-1929 Ashcan/Impressionist NYC street paintings and drawings by artists safely in the US public domain (published pre-1929 or author died >70 years ago).
round3.sourcing_note: With Manhattan allowed, the field is much richer and there are now several CLEAN public-domain ILLUSTRATIONS of NYC brick/brownstone residential blocks - no borderline WPA/FAP licence needed. The strongest LITERAL 'stoop + iron railing + brick facade' image (Shinn, 'Winter on 21st Street') is unfortunately only available at low resolution; the best-quality clean colour options (Coleman, Cornoyer, Hassam) read as brick-row streets and tree-lined Village blocks rather than a tight close-up of a stooped brownstone. All six candidates below are genuine hand-made illustrations (oil, pastel, pencil), none are photographs, and every one is clean US public domain - no licence doubt this round. Rejected the FAP colour lithograph route (Met 'Front Row' by Dayton Brandfield turned out to be a cinema interior, not houses) and the Met Coleman 'New York Street Scene' (near-monochrome crowded market plaza, not a row).
round3.licence_note: No borderline licences this round. Coleman d.1932 (works 1927 & 1929, published pre-1929/PD), Sloan d.1951 (1914 work, pre-1929/PD), Cornoyer d.1923 (clean PD-old-100), Hassam d.1935 (1890 work, pre-1929/PD), Shinn d.1953 (c.1899-1900 work, pre-1929/PD), Myers d.1940 (1911 dated CC0; 'East 22nd Street' undated but PD by author death, life+70 expired 2011). Whitney/NGA/Met open-access sources corroborate PD/CC0.

also_investigated_and_rejected: Henry Farrer, 'Scenes of Old New York' etchings (Met CC0, 1870s: 'Old House in Rector Street', 'Peck Slip & Water St', 'The Old Beach House cor. Cedar & Greenwich'): clean CC0 illustrations of OLD Manhattan houses, but they depict individual quaint colonial/federal wood-and-brick houses, not brownstone/brick ROWS with stoops - weak fit (~3/10).
Glenn O. Coleman, 'New York Street Scene' (Met 1983.86.1, CC0, 1929): near-monochrome oil of a crowded market plaza with food carts and an el, not a residential row.
Dayton Brandfield, 'Front Row' (Met, colour FAP lithograph, PD): title is misleading - it is the front row of a CINEMA interior, no houses.
Childe Hassam, 'New York Street' (Art Institute of Chicago, 1902): clean PD colour, but it is a snowy park edge with bare trees and figures - no row houses.

Jerome Myers, 'New York Street Scene' (NGA, CC0, 1911): clean high-res monochrome drawing of a Lower East Side tenement corner storefront ('27 1/2') with balconies and laundry - good 'old brick NYC' but a tenement corner rather than a stooped brownstone row (kept 'East 22nd Street' instead as the better-stooped Myers).
Everett Shinn, 'Fifth Avenue' (Brooklyn Museum): PD colour, but an avenue/traffic scene, not a residential row.
'Striver's Row' and West Side / 104th-St / 89th-St row-house images on Commons: genuine brownstone rows but all modern PHOTOGRAPHS (disallowed by the illustration rule).
round3.recommendation: Top NEW pick: cornoyer-washington-square.jpg (Paul Cornoyer, 'Washington Square', 1900). It is the best CLEAN-LICENCE COLOUR illustration that matches the relaxed brief - a tree-lined Greenwich Village residential block with the sunlit red-brick 'Row' of Washington Square North, warm and characterful, unambiguous public domain, at a usable (if not large) 1280x934. If maximum image quality matters more than leafiness, coleman-street-scene-lower-new-york.jpg (clean colour, 1242x1500) is the strongest high-resolution 'brick row houses' street. And if a tight, literal stoop-and-iron-railing read is the priority, shinn-winter-21st-street-chelsea.jpg is the single best subject match of the entire search - the only caveat being its low 768x638 resolution. For a monochrome alternative, myers-east-22nd-street.jpg gives clean high-res stooped Gramercy doorways. Net: this round DOES beat the existing options for the relaxed 'brick row houses / brownstones' aesthetic - Cornoyer, Coleman and Shinn are all cleaner-licence and more on-aesthetic than the borderline WPA Nooney or the wood-frame Guy scenes, so a Manhattan pick is recommended.

round4.brief: More options specifically from CHELSEA or the WEST VILLAGE / Greenwich Village, Manhattan, reading as brownstone / brick row-house streets (stoops, iron railings, tree-lined residential blocks, red-brick or brownstone facades). Prefer COLOUR and >1000px; a strong monochrome print acceptable if the subject is a clear brownstone/townhouse row. Try to beat the low resolution (768px) of the round-3 Shinn Chelsea pastel with a larger clean-PD colour Village/Chelsea street.
round4.sources_searched: Wikimedia Commons (search + artist queries), The Met Open Access API, National Gallery of Art open access (via Commons), Smithsonian American Art Museum (via Commons), Whitney/New Britain/Google Art Project donations on Commons. Targeted Ashcan and American Impressionist painters of Village/Chelsea streets who are US public domain (pre-1929 works or artist dead >70 years): Everett Shinn, John Sloan, William Glackens, Glenn O. Coleman, Ernest Lawson, Paul Cornoyer, Childe Hassam, plus Charles Mielatz etchings and Beulah Bettersworth.
round4.sourcing_note: With Chelsea/West Village as the focus there is one genuinely strong NEW subject - Beulah Bettersworth's 'Christopher Street, Greenwich Village' - a colour West Village winter street of brick row buildings with a corner stoop, at good resolution (native 1601x2000, saved 1201x1500), which clearly BEATS the low-res Shinn Chelsea pastel on both size and colour. Its only weakness is the licence basis (a 1934 Public Works of Art Project canvas, held by the Smithsonian American Art Museum; PD is claimed via PD-USGov-Treasury because the PWAP was a federal Treasury programme - a reasonably solid rationale that Commons and SAAM accept, but it rests on the federal-work argument rather than author death, since Bettersworth died 1968). Everything else clean-PD this round reads as a Washington Square PARK/ARCH scene (Glackens, Coleman) or a Chelsea ROOFTOP genre scene (Sloan) or an ambiguous downtown brick CANYON (Lawson) rather than a tight stooped townhouse row - useful colour Village/Chelsea data points, but none is a better literal 'brownstone row' than Bettersworth. No clean-PD COLOUR Chelsea RESIDENTIAL ROW at high resolution surfaced; Chelsea's best clean options remain rooftops (Sloan) or the round-3 Shinn street. Mielatz's NGA NYC etching set (CC0) covers Cherry St, Wall St, Madison Sq, Central Park - no Village/Chelsea row. Rejected the Sloan 'Sixth Avenue and Thirtieth Street' (el/commercial, not a residential row) and the Hassam Fifth-Avenue-at-23rd etching (a monochrome Flatiron canyon, no houses).
round4.licence_note: Glackens d.1938 (1912 work, pre-1929/PD - clean), Sloan d.1951 (1915 work, pre-1929/PD - clean), Coleman d.1932 (1927 work, pre-1929/PD - clean), Lawson d.1939 (pre-1929 work; PD - clean). Bettersworth d.1968: her 1934 canvas is PD only via the PWAP/US-Treasury federal-work rationale (PD-USGov-Treasury on Commons; SAAM lists it as their collection) - honest caveat, treat as PD-with-a-federal-work-basis rather than PD-by-author-death.

candidates.brownstone_rating: 4/10 - a sunlit Chelsea rooftop genre scene: a woman in a white dress hanging washing, with a warm RED-BRICK Chelsea facade and windowed brick blocks across the backyard behind. Genuinely Chelsea and clean colour, but the figure dominates and it shows rooftops/brick backs rather than a stooped street front - the best clean-licence CHELSEA colour option this round despite the weak 'row' read.
candidates.note: Only clean-PD colour CHELSEA candidate found this round; a rooftop rather than a street row. Companion 'Red Kimono on the Roof' (1912, 2010x2656) is similar and available if a variant is wanted.

candidates.brownstone_rating: 5/10 - a moody colour canyon of tall old BRICK buildings lining a street that recedes to a hazy skyline, with figures, a horse-cart and an awning. Strong 'old brick New York street' atmosphere and high resolution, but it reads as a downtown/commercial brick canyon of ambiguous location, not a leafy Chelsea/Village residential row.
candidates.note: High-resolution clean-PD colour brick street, but neighbourhood is uncertain and it is a canyon rather than a townhouse row - included as an honest colour data point.

also_investigated_and_rejected: John Sloan, 'Red Kimono on the Roof' (1912, 2010x2656, clean PD colour): a second Chelsea rooftop laundry scene, essentially a variant of 'Sun and Wind on the Roof' - kept the latter as the representative Chelsea rooftop.
John Sloan, 'Sixth Avenue and Thirtieth Street' (1907, 1500x1201, clean PD colour): el/commercial Sixth Avenue with a tenement corner, not a residential brownstone row.
Childe Hassam, 'Washington's Birthday - Fifth Avenue at 23rd Street' (1916 etching, 1369x2400): a MONOCHROME Flatiron/Fifth Avenue canyon of traffic, no row houses.
Childe Hassam, 'Fifth Avenue in Winter' (c.1892): low resolution (839x640) and an avenue rather than a residential row.

Paul Cornoyer, 'Washington Square in Winter': clean-PD colour and shows the Washington Square North row in snow, but duplicates the artist AND the Washington Square subject already used in round 3 (cornoyer-washington-square.jpg).

Glackens 'Washington Square' 1910 (New Britain), 'Early Spring, Washington Square', '29 Washington Square': all clean PD but low resolution (600-850px) and same square subject; kept the larger 1912 'Washington Square' (1252px) instead.

Charles F. W. Mielatz NGA etching set (CC0: 'Cherry Street', 'St. Paul's Broadway', 'A Rainy Night Madison Square', 'Bit of Central Park', 'Porch, Old Custom House'): clean high-res CC0 illustrations of NYC, but none depicts a Village/Chelsea residential row (Cherry Street is a Lower East Side tenement block).
Genuine Chelsea/West Village brownstone-row images on Commons (Christopher Street, Grove Court, MacDougal Alley, Washington Mews): all modern PHOTOGRAPHS, disallowed by the illustration rule.
round4.recommendation: Top NEW pick: bettersworth-christopher-street-west-village.jpg (Beulah Bettersworth, 'Christopher Street, Greenwich Village', 1934, SAAM). It is the round's one genuinely strong result: a COLOUR West Village street of brick row buildings with a corner stoop, at usable resolution (1201x1500) that clearly BEATS the low-res round-3 Shinn Chelsea pastel on both size and colour. Its only caveat is the licence basis - a 1934 PWAP federal-Treasury commission, PD via PD-USGov-Treasury (Commons/SAAM accept it) rather than author death (artist d.1968) - so it should be flagged, though this rationale is sturdier than the round-2 WPA/FAP Nooney case. If a STRICTLY clean author-death/pre-1929 licence is required, the best NEW colour Village option is glackens-washington-square-village.jpg (clean PD, 1252px, red-brick Village frontage by a new Ashcan artist), with coleman-the-arch-washington-square.jpg as a bolder high-res Village alternative and sloan-sun-wind-roof-chelsea.jpg as the only clean-PD COLOUR Chelsea option (a rooftop, not a row). Net for CHELSEA specifically: nothing new beats the round-3 Shinn 21st-Street street as a literal Chelsea ROW - Chelsea's clean-PD colour options remain rooftops. For the WEST VILLAGE, Bettersworth is the new front-runner and Glackens the clean-licence runner-up.
